verses.text: The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin! The LORD is with you as long as you are with him. If you look for him, you will find him. But if you leave him, he will leave you.
For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach them, and without the law.
But when they were in trouble and turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and looked for him, they found him.
In those days it was not safe for anyone to travel. Great trouble was on everyone who lived in those lands.
Nation fought against nation and town against town, because God troubled them with every kind of hardship.
But you, be strong! Do not give up, because your work will be rewarded."

When Asa heard these words, the message of Oded the prophet, he became brave. He removed the disgusting idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He repaired the LORD's altar in front of the porch of the LORD's temple.

He gathered all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were living among them. Many people had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule.
That day they offered sacrifices to the LORD from the loot they had brought back: seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep.
They made a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and all their soul.
Anyone who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.
They made a promise to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, and with trumpets and horns.
All Judah was happy about the promise, because they had promised with all their heart. They looked for the LORD with all their desire, and they found him. So the LORD gave them peace on every side.

King Asa also removed his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother, because she had made a disgusting idol for the goddess Asherah. Asa cut down the idol, crushed it to dust, and burned it at the Kidron Valley.
The hilltop shrines were not removed from Israel, but Asa's heart was fully faithful all his life.
He brought into God's temple the silver, gold, and other objects that he and his father had set apart for God.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
